subject: english-literature
title: Sound Effects of Language
welcome_lead: Some devices work on the ear as much as the mind.
meta_desc: KS3 English Literature adventure on alliteration, onomatopoeia and sound devices.
final_note: You can now hear how writers tune their sentences.

concepts.def: Same starting sound on nearby words.
Word that sounds like its meaning.
Same end sound on two words.

walkthroughs.body_html: 'Slithering, silent serpents' uses alliteration — repeated starting sound builds rhythm or mood.
'Crash', 'buzz', 'hiss' — words that sound like what they describe. Comic books love them.
Sibilance uses 's' or soft 'sh' sounds. It can suggest secrets, snakes or whispers.

mcqs.q: What are conventions of the Gothic genre?
options: Genre means whether a book is fiction or non-fiction.
Settings of ruin and decay, supernatural or psychological terror, transgression of boundaries, the sublime, doubled or haunted protagonists, and atmospheric excess.
Gothic just means scary stories with vampires and ghosts.
Gothic refers to medieval architecture, not literature.
A line of five iambs (unstressed-stressed syllable pairs), creating a ten-syllable line with the rhythm da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM da-DUM.
Iambic pentameter is any line with ten syllables.
Iambic pentameter is when every line rhymes.
Gothic refers to medieval architecture, not literature.

mcqs.q: Why are genre conventions important when interpreting a text?
options: Genre means whether a book is fiction or non-fiction.
They set reader expectations the text can fulfil or subvert; analysing how a text uses or breaks conventions reveals its meaning and significance.
Genre is just a label to help bookshops categorise novels.
Iambic pentameter is when every line rhymes.
